title: Condensation temperature and magnetic phases of trapped coherently coupled Bose gases
authors: Sunilkumar V, Rajat, Sandeep Gautam, Arko Roy
abstract: We investigate condensation and finite-temperature magnetic phase transitions in a coherently (Rabi) coupled Bose gas confined in a three-dimensional harmonic trap. For the noninteracting system, we derive analytical expressions for the critical temperature and condensate fraction using a semiclassical description of the single-particle spectrum and density of states. At fixed particle number, coherent coupling enhances the critical temperature relative to the uncoupled system, and this enhancement decreases with increasing particle number $N$. The finite-size correction, in contrast, lowers the transition temperature, with its effect diminishing for larger $N$. We then incorporate repulsive interactions within the Hartree--Fock--Bogoliubov--Popov framework to investigate the finite-temperature phase diagram in the temperature--Rabi coupling plane. The system undergoes successive transitions from a ferromagnetic to a paramagnetic condensate and, at higher temperature, to a thermal gas. The transition boundaries obtained from the vanishing of the condensate fraction show excellent agreement with the analytical Hartree-Fock predictions. We find that the interactions substantially suppress the variation in the condensation temperature with an increase in the coherent coupling.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the phase transitions and critical temperature of a Bose gas coupled coherently in a harmonic trap. By using semiclassical and HFB-Popov methods, the authors show that coherent coupling modifies $T_c$, and that repulsive interactions stabilize the system's response to this coupling. The results provide a detailed phase diagram mapping the transition from magnetic to thermal states.
main_problem: The paper investigates the condensation temperature and magnetic phase transitions in a Bose gas subjected to coherent coupling (Rabi coupling) within a harmonic trap.
main_result: Coherent coupling enhances the critical temperature, and repulsive interactions substantially suppress the variation of this temperature with increasing coupling strength.
method: The study employs the semiclassical description for the noninteracting case and the Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov–Popov (HFB-Popov) framework for interactions.
model_or_system: The system is a Bose gas confined in a 3D harmonic trap, modeled with a Hamiltonian incorporating a coherent coupling term ($\sigma_x$). The analysis covers both noninteracting and interacting regimes.
key_observables: Critical temperature ($T_c$), condensate fraction ($N_0/N$), and the magnetic phase diagram (Ferromagnetic $	o$ Paramagnetic $	o$ Thermal gas).
important_parameters: Coherent coupling strength ($\Omega$), particle number ($N$), and interaction strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The semiclassical approximation ($k_B T \gg \hbar\omega$) is used for the density of states, and the analysis incorporates finite-size corrections.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the excitation spectrum showing level splitting, the density of states ($ho_{3D}, ho_{2D}$) for varying coupling, and the normalized $T_c$ and condensate fraction versus temperature.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from noninteracting analysis using semiclassical methods to incorporating finite-size corrections. It then extends the analysis to include repulsive interactions using the HFB-Popov framework to map the full phase diagram.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the interplay between coherent quantum coupling, spatial confinement, and interatomic interactions on fundamental quantum phase transitions in ultracold atomic systems.

(b) Two-dimensional DOS, ρ2D, exhibiting the char- acteristic linear dependence on energy for different coherent coupling strengths.

FIG. 3. Variation of the critical temperature and condensate fraction of a three-dimensional ideal coherently coupled BEC. (a) Normalized critical temperature, Tc(Ω)/Tc(0), as a func- tion of coherent coupling strength for different atom numbers. The enhancement of Tc becomes less pronounced with increas- ing N. (b) Condensate fraction, N0/N, as a function of the scaled temperature, T/Tc(0), for different atom numbers at Ω/ω = 10. For each atom number N, the temperature is nor- malized separately by its corresponding zero-coupling critical temperature.
